title: The Template Textbook
description:
A modular, fillable scaffold for book-length technical works: a data-driven manuscript (parts/chapters/labs/questions), a tested computational backbone, deterministic figures and Mermaid diagrams, and a content scaffold/validation engine.

methods.name: Single config.yaml source of truth for book structure
methods.description: Parts, chapters, front matter, appendices, labs and question banks are declared in config.yaml, from which TOC, numbering and integrity tests read.
methods.evidence: The whole book is data-driven from a single source of truth, config.yaml. That file declares the parts, the chapters inside each part, the front matter, the appendices, and the labs and question banks.

methods.name: Tested Python backbone (textbook.models) and deterministic figures
methods.description: Worked equations are implemented as tested Python functions that chapter prose calls, and figures are generated deterministically from code.
methods.evidence: A tested computational backbone in src/ — the worked equations are real, tested Python func- tions (textbook.models), and figures are generated deterministically.

methods.name: Pandoc + pandoc-crossref rendering pipeline
methods.description: The manuscript is assembled from Markdown in declared order after analysis scripts produce figures, then rendered to PDF via Pandoc with pandoc-crossref.
methods.evidence: The pipeline reads config.yaml, runs the analysis scripts that produce figures and diagrams, assembles the Markdown sections in declared order, and renders a PDF through Pandoc with pandoc-crossref resolving every cross-reference and citation.

methods.name: Stub-marker counting audit and manuscript-integrity tests
methods.description: A quality audit counts STUB/TODO/TKTK markers and pytest checks the per-chapter content contract, unique labels, citations and glossary anchors.
methods.evidence: tests/test_manuscript_integrity.py verifies that every chapter satisfies the content contract, that labels are unique, that citations resolve, and that glossary links point at real anchors.

methods.name: Two filled worked-reference chapters (logistic growth; dose-response)
methods.description: First Principles derives the logistic growth law; Case Studies fits a linear dose-response trend to a small synthetic six-condition dataset.
methods.evidence: This chapter is a worked reference in a different style from sec. 8: where that chapter derives a model, this one applies one to a small dataset. The remaining chapters ship as stubs.

key_findings: The book is explicitly a scaffold rather than a finished work: every structural element is present and author-specific passages are marked stubs.
It provides twelve chapter shells across four parts, each with a matching lab and question bank.
Claims building the book reproduces byte-identical figures and numbers, since nothing in the prose is computed by hand.
The worked case study's linear fit gives slope 1.375 and R2 = 0.999, while warning that three averaged points cannot support prediction or extrapolation.
key_findings_evidence: This is not a finished book. It is a scaffold — a complete, internally consistent skeleton for a book-length technical work, with every structural element in place and every author-specific passage left as a marked stub for you to fill.

Twelve chapters across four parts, each a valid chapter shell with a labelled heading, a figure, a metadata badge, a Study Blueprint, Learning Objectives, a worked formalism (equation + parameter table)

Every equation in this book is implemented as a tested function and every figure is generated deterministically from code. Nothing in the prose is computed by hand. If you build the book yourself you will get byte- identical figures and numbers
A linear fit through three averaged points reports 𝑅2 = 0.999, but that number describes how well the line passes through three dots — not how well it predicts the next exper- iment.

summary_provenance.method: Evidence-grounded extraction from full_text.md: every method and finding carries a verbatim quote from the paper text, mechanically verified to occur in full_text.md (whitespace/ligature-normalized) before merge.
summary_provenance.notes: Template/scaffold textbook: most chapters are stubs and the bibliography consists of placeholder references; the case-study data are explicitly synthetic. Findings describe the scaffold's design, not research results. full_text.md is extracted from one of three PDFs in the folder (Friedman_2026_Template_c6c97f24.pdf).
